- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:218-220 | severity=low | confidence=5

- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:853-854 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The same stale "tg_send_msg's curl has no time limit" comment sits in `promote_cycle_hold_alert`, although `tg_send_msg` now stops itself at 30 seconds.
  WHY: This maintenance hazard is the same as in scripts/auto_release_stable.sh: the abandonment loop is now a second bound, not the only one (all reviewers rated it NIT, mapped to low).
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:1176-1177 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The same stale "tg_send_msg's curl has no time limit" comment sits in `release_blocker_alert`, although `tg_send_msg` now stops itself at 30 seconds.
  WHY: The comment gives a false reason for the background-and-abandon logic and could mislead future work on that timeout path (all reviewers rated it NIT, mapped to low).
- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:146-147 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The new `--max-time 30` on `tg_send_msg`'s curl contradicts the existing caller comments in `scripts/auto_release_stable.sh` and `scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh`, which say the curl has no time limit.
  WHY: This is a documentation defect: a future maintainer may remove the abandonment logic based on a false assumption and bring the stalls back (both reviewers rated it NIT, mapped to low).
- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:106 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_tg_chat_id` is called in a subshell without suppressing stderr.
  WHY: Any warnings `_tg_chat_id` prints to stderr (for example when a secret is missing) would pollute log-parsing that greps stderr (rated NIT, mapped to low; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash separately disputed a similar stderr finding at line 110, saying `_tg_chat_id` cannot emit stderr).
- scripts/tg_helpers.sh:154 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: When Telegram returns a response without a `message_id` (for example `ok:false`), `tg_send_msg` silently returns an empty string.
  WHY: Callers treat the empty id as a delivery failure, so an operator cannot tell a network timeout from a Telegram API rejection (rated NIT, mapped to low; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same point as a hardening suggestion, not a finding).

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
(No findings reported.)
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: scripts/tg_helpers.sh, tg_send_msg, after line 155 (`msg_id=$(printf '%s' "${resp}" | jq -r '.result.message_id // empty' 2>/dev/null)`)
  PROBLEM: When Telegram answers `ok:false`, `tg_send_msg` prints an empty id with no warning, unlike `tg_send_report_msg` (lines 190-192), so the P6b callers can only log `send_failed_or_ambiguous`.
  WHY: An operator cannot tell a curl timeout from a Telegram rejection, and that parking is never paged again. Suggested fix: print the sanitized `::warning::Telegram returned no message id: <description>` to stderr, as at line 192. Estimated 3 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- NOTE: The stale "tg_send_msg's curl has no time limit" comments (confirmed at scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:218, scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:853 and :1176) are outside files_touched and nothing fails at runtime, so the reviewer did not raise them as a finding.
- NOTE: The copilot-pull-request-reviewer CI failure is external (`custom_instructions_too_large`, HTTP 422), 6 check-runs were still incomplete, and the tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py failure does not trace to this diff.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
